issue: Grammar tip is factually muddled: 'yang can point back to a whole action' misdescribes an object relative clause — yang refers to the noun (baju), not to an action. Sentence itself is fine.

fix.target: Baju yang kamu beli kemarin bagus sekali.
fix.english: The shirt that you bought yesterday is really nice.
fix.grammar: yang also links a noun to what someone did to it: baju yang kamu beli = the shirt that you bought.

issue: English-calque collocation: 'bus yang pergi ke bandara' — pergi is for people; natives say 'bus yang ke bandara' or 'bus jurusan bandara' for a route.

fix.target: Bus yang ke bandara berangkat jam enam.
fix.english: The bus that goes to the airport leaves at six.

issue: Same calque as id-0311: 'bus yang pergi ke stasiun' — vehicles are not said to pergi; the natural route phrasing is 'bus yang ke stasiun'.

fix.target: Ini bus yang ke stasiun, bukan?
fix.english: This is the bus that goes to the station, isn't it?

issue: Clunky double 'bulan': 'Bulan Desember bulan paling sibuk' — the zero-copula equational with the repeated noun reads awkwardly; needs adalah or the first bulan dropped.

fix.target: Desember adalah bulan paling sibuk untuk kami.
fix.english: December is the busiest month for us.

issue: Deixis clash: 'Kamar ini ... di hotel itu' — pointing at THIS room while calling the hotel you are standing in THAT hotel is incoherent; gloss faithfully copies the clash.

fix.target: Kamar ini yang paling murah di hotel ini.
fix.english: This room is the cheapest one in this hotel.

issue: Gloss fidelity: bare 'adik' glossed as 'little sibling is sleeping' — unnatural English with no possessor; add 'saya' to the target so both sides match cleanly.

fix.target: Jangan bicara keras-keras, adik saya sedang tidur.
fix.english: Don't talk loudly, my little sibling is sleeping.

issue: Clipped comment 'tidak baik' with no subject is stiff textbook Indonesian; a native warning uses nanti + consequence.

fix.target: Jangan makan terlalu cepat, nanti sakit perut.
fix.english: Don't eat too fast, you will get a stomachache.
fix.grammar: nanti in a warning means 'or else': nanti sakit perut = you'll get a stomachache.

issue: Unnatural collocation: 'menu makanannya' is redundant — in a restaurant you ask for 'menunya', never 'menu makanan'.

fix.english: May I have the menu, ma'am?

issue: Imperative drops the -i suffix: mencicipi's imperative is 'cicipi'; bare 'cicip' is Jakarta-colloquial clipping (offender in Q1-Q3). Only the meN- prefix drops in requests, not verb suffixes.

fix.target: Coba cicipi sup ini, rasanya enak sekali.
fix.english: Try a taste of this soup, it tastes really good.

issue: English-calque location: 'berfoto di depan pantai' (in front of the beach) is not a natural place phrase — natives take photos 'di pantai' or 'di pinggir pantai'; the odd English gloss mirrors the calque.

fix.target: Mari kita berfoto bersama di pantai.
fix.english: Let's take a photo together at the beach.
fix.grammar: ber- turns a noun into 'do X': berfoto = take a photo.

issue: Tense mismatch: with no time anchor, 'Saya mandi dulu' defaults to a present intention ('I'll shower first'), but the gloss is past; the tip's own example even glosses it present ('I shower first'), contradicting the card.

fix.target: Tadi pagi saya mandi dulu, lalu sarapan dengan keluarga.
fix.english: This morning I showered first, then had breakfast with my family.
fix.grammar: dulu after a verb means 'first': mandi dulu = shower first, before anything else.

issue: Bookish register for Q2: 'hujan turun sangat deras' is written-narrative prose; in conversation natives say 'hujan deras sekali'.

fix.english: Yesterday morning it rained really hard.

issue: Broken collocation: 'tidur larut' is clipped — the set phrase is 'tidur larut malam', which would clash with 'tadi malam'; the natural single word for staying up late is 'begadang'.

fix.target: Tadi malam saya begadang karena pekerjaan.
fix.english: Last night I stayed up late because of work.
fix.grammar: begadang = stay up late into the night — one everyday word, no extra phrase needed.

issue: English calque: 'saya merasa pusing' copies 'I feel dizzy' — natives state symptoms directly ('saya pusing'); merasa here is stiff clinic-form language for Q2.

fix.target: Pagi ini saya pusing dan mual.
fix.english: This morning I feel dizzy and nauseous.
